How many of you shop regularly on Myntra? 👀

Do you actually use the Wishlist feature?

✅ Wishlist shows price drop alerts, so you know if the discount is real or inflated
✅ Myntra often drops prices 5–10% more after you add items to your wishlist
✅ Easy to track, compare, and buy at the lowest point instead of rushing

Pro tip:
Even during sale days
 👉 add the product to wishlist first, wait a bit, track the price… then buy 😉

Small habit. Extra savings.

text:
A consumer who speaks up is stronger than a company that avoids accountability. 

Arjun had saved his hard-earned money with great hope and ordered an expensive jacket worth ₹26,000 from Myntra. When the parcel arrived, he was excited. But the moment he opened the box, his happiness turned into shock.

Instead of the ₹26,000 jacket, the package contained a pair of shorts worth barely ₹150.

Imagine what he must have felt. His money was gone, his trust was broken, and all he received was disappointment.

Arjun immediately initiated a return. Days turned into weeks, and weeks into months, but his refund never arrived. Every time he contacted customer support, he received the same response: “Sir, we are investigating the matter.” He was forced to repeatedly follow up just to recover his own money, causing immense stress and sleepless nights.

But Arjun refused to give up. Instead of accepting the situation, he approached the Consumer Court.

During the hearing, the company argued that the mistake was not theirs but the seller's.

However, the court made it clear that the customer had placed his trust in the platform and paid the platform. The company could not escape responsibility by blaming a third-party seller.

The verdict was significant. The court ordered Myntra to refund the full ₹26,000 and also pay ₹50,000 as compensation for the mental harassment caused to the customer.

This case sends an important message: online platforms cannot avoid responsibility by shifting the blame to sellers. When customers purchase through a platform, the platform is accountable for resolving such issues.

A valuable lesson for every online shopper: always record an unboxing video when receiving expensive items such as phones, laptops, or branded clothing. It can serve as crucial evidence if something goes wrong.

If you ever face a similar issue, don't stay silent. You can file a complaint through the National Consumer Helpline (1915) or submit a case online through the e-Daakhil portal.

Arjun Kumar's determination is an inspiration for millions of consumers who often feel powerless against large companies. His fight is a reminder that consumers have rights—and with persistence, justice can prevail.

FRACTAL INDUSTRIES SME IPO BUSINESS REVIEW.  LOOKS GOOD. MENS WEAR  🌟AVOIDED due to lack of clarity on scaling, on other B2C Platforms. Will consider LATER.   MUMBAI based garment manufacturer. Sells mainly on Myntra (95%) . Also 95% sale is from shirts and trousers. Other products are namesake.   
🩷LIKE, READ FULL REVIEW & DECIDE

This business review is based on DRHP/RHP filed by the company at Exchange & is based on reviewer’s understanding of the documentation. For a full understanding of risks, financials, objectives & prospects suggest to go through the RHP in detail & form own opinion.

OBJECTS:
Out of Rs.49 Cr Raised, Rs.36.5Cr for working capital and rest for general and listing expenses

BRICKWORK Rating has been retained for IPO fund usage monitoring.

BUSINESS & PROSPECTS:
98% of garments manufactured are shirts and trousers. They have negligible presence in other items. 95% is sold at Myntra and 5% at Flipkart

Manufacturing unit is located at Mumbai with warehouses located in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Haryana, West Bengal and Karnataka. Capacity is 4,40,000 units per year. About 65% utilization
FY25 revenue was Rs.85Cr 👍  Rs.36.5Cr for WC should help in substantial growth in Fy27

RISK & CONJECTURE:
The company has been very successful in spreading its sales on Myntra (Shirts & Trousers) contributing 95% of revenue. Basically there is Single Platform Risk. We have to wonder why it is so when it is easy to sell  on all 3 major platforms (Flipkart, Myntra and Amazon) . Our theory is that company could be  legally constrained by its terms of agreement with Myntra. (This is only a logical assumption considering 95% sale on Myntra. Small 5% sale on Flipkart could be non core items. ie other than Menswear) If this is true, then growth will be slow and steady. NOT SURE. NO mention of this aspect in RHP.

VALUATION AND DECISION:
Rs.216 is at 16x   its TTM earnings, on post IPO equity basis.
Karnika Industries (Rs.170Cr turnover) which make Children's wear and came up with IPO at 11p/e at Rs.78 had moved  above Rs.200. Currently Rs.145 at 36 p/e.

If Fractal can grow towards 200Cr without any exclusivity constrains put on it by customers, then it should also do well in the market👍

However, at the moment due to lack of enough info, will SKIP and consider LATER

Suggest to assess  yourself and take your own decision, after further study, considering various factors discussed and any other info available.

text:
Enforcement Directorate / 1600 crores / Myntra 

Directorate of Enforcement (ED), Bengaluru Zonal Office has filed a complaint u/s 16(3) of Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA) against M/s. Myntra Designs Private Limited (Myntra) and its related companies and their Directors for contravention to the tune of Rs. 1654,35,08,981/

The enquiries in the matter were initiated on the basis of a credible information that *M/s. Myntra Designs Private Limited (Myntra) and its related companies are doing Multi Brand Retail Trade (MBRT) in the guise of ‘Wholesale Cash & Carry’*, allegedly in violation of the extant FDI Policy. 
ED investigation under the provisions of FEMA, 1999 revealed that M/s. Myntra Designs Pvt. Ltd. had declared that they were engaged in the business of wholesale cash & carry and invited and received FDI from foreign investors equivalent to Rs 1654,35,08,981/- and that they sold majority of their goods to M/s. Vector E-Commerce Pvt. Ltd.  (who sold the goods in retail to the ultimate customer). That M/s. Vector E-Commerce Pvt. Ltd. and M/s. Myntra Designs Pvt. Ltd are related parties and belong to same group or group of companies.
M/s Vector E-Commerce Pvt. Ltd. was created and continued to be used as corporate entity to bifurcate the B2C [(business to customer i.e. Myntra Designs Pvt. Ltd. to retail customers)] transaction into B2B (Myntra Designs Pvt. Ltd. to Vector E-Commerce Pvt. Ltd.) and then B2C (Vector E-Commerce Pvt. Ltd. to retail customers);
ED investigation alsoy revealed that Myntra Designs Pvt. Ltd. was actually carrying out multi-brand retail trading in the guise of wholesale cash & carry. Even otherwise, Myntra Designs Pvt. Ltd. have not satisfied the condition laid down for “Wholesale/Cash & Carry Trading” as they have made cent per cent sales to Vector E-Commerce Pvt. Ltd which is in contravention of amendment dated 01.04.2010 and 01.10.2010 which permitted only 25% sale to companies belonging to the same group or group companies. Myntra Designs Pvt. Ltd. and others have contravened the provisions as per section 6(3)(b) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 and Consolidated FDI Policy dated 01.04.2010 and Consolidated FDI Policy dated 01.10.2010 to the tune of Rs. 1654,35,08,981/-. 
In view of the above, a complaint u/s 16 (3) of FEMA, 1999 is filed before the Adjudicating Authority under FEMA.
